verdict.rationale: Keycloak's first-party docs describe dedicated Authorization Services that go beyond role-based authorization. These cover protected resources as first-class objects, centrally defined policies and permissions, UMA permission tickets, a Protection API, and management of access to user-owned resources. That squarely covers resource-level, policy-based authorization. Missing for 10: specific policy types beyond role-based (e.g. attribute, time or user policies) are not named in the evidence, relationship-based (ReBAC) modeling is not evidenced, and there is no independent or hands-on corroboration.
